HSTU already supports sampled-softmax training: Meta’s released MovieLens configuration uses 128 negatives, temperature 0.05, and normalized user/item embeddings. This supports changing the objective or sampler while retaining HSTU, but does not establish optimal settings for Amazon Electronics. Large margins against easy negatives alone cannot establish ranking generalization. [Official HSTU configuration](https://github.com/meta-recsys/generative-recommenders/blob/main/configs/ml-1m/hstu-sampled-softmax-n128-final.gin)

LogQ correction addresses sampling bias, especially the disproportionate use of popular items as in-batch negatives. The 2025 paper *Correcting the LogQ Correction* identifies an additional distinction: the positive is always included, rather than sampled, and derives a revised correction. Therefore, do not blindly subtract the same logQ term from every logit; correction must match the actual sampling scheme. Hard-negative selection changes that scheme further. [RecSys 2025 paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331)

Practical hypothesis: compare larger uniform-negative sampled softmax against a uniform-plus-moderately-hard objective, mining with the same HSTU network after warm-up. Exclude known training positives and duplicate candidates; retain random negatives rather than selecting only the highest-scoring items. These are proposed ablations, not demonstrated improvements: Hard-BPR finds that hard sampling can amplify false-negative damage and motivates a robust objective. Unknown relevance remains unknown; high scores do not prove negative labels. Keep one model per category, fixed seeds and training limits, and select by the prescribed four-category macro validation HR@10, examining Electronics separately. [Hard-BPR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19276)
